text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Murtaza Bhutto's supporters clash with Pakistani police, blocking a condolence call by President Farooq Leghari.
- Singapore government pleased with high take-up rate for second batch of discounted Singapore Telecom shares.
- President Suharto of Indonesia scheduled to visit Malaysia to meet Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad to discuss bilateral matters including disputes over Sipadan and Ligitan islands.
- Thailand's ruling coalition begins to look for a new leader and bargain for shares in a new government.
- Wing Tai announces 73 per cent jump in group net earnings to $145 million as turnover climbs 53 per cent to $573 million for the year ended June 30.
- Analysts say planned resignation of Thai Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa and subsequent formation of new administration will lead to better economic policies.
- The eastern part of Singapore has lowest take-up for new homes according to a Business Times survey.
- Three of Asia's biggest conglomerates are joining a Singapore-promoted US$200 million industrual development project in Burma.
